name: RDM
description: Representation Distribution Matching (RDM / iRDM) is a paradigm for training state-of-the-art one-step visual generation models developed by EPFL (VITA Lab), Valeo.ai, and Sorbonne Université. It matches feature distributions between generated and reference images using Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) with Nyström estimation across a battery of frozen pretrained encoders.
keyFeatures: Representation Distribution Matching (RDM): Matches feature distributions of generated images to real image distributions using frozen pretrained visual encoders.
Improved RDM (iRDM): Scalable objective combining within-batch repulsion with Nyström landmark estimation for efficient attraction to reference embeddings.
Multi-Encoder Battery Defense: Employs a balanced battery of frozen encoders (evaluated via SW_r14) to prevent representation gaming.
Single-Step FLUX.2 Distillation: Post-trains multi-step models (e.g. FLUX.2 Klein) into 1-step generators outperforming 4-step teachers.
Large Batch Scaling: Utilizes large batch sizes (>2048) to stabilize MMD estimation and maximize single-step visual quality.
curatorNotes: Verified paper arXiv:2607.02375 and open-source project from EPFL (VITA Lab), Valeo.ai, and Sorbonne Université. Project page hosted at alan-lanfeng.github.io/rdm/, GitHub at vita-epfl/RDM, Hugging Face model and demo space available.
